content.title: Bianca Belair Shocks The World With Pregnancy Announcement At WrestleMania 42
content.text: Bianca Belair announced her pregnancy at WrestleMania 42.WWEBianca Belair Is Pregnant | Key Points Bianca Belair made her return to WWE, and announced her pregnancy. Bianca has not had a match since the opening match of WrestleMania 41, Night 2. “The EST is having a baby!” Bianca announced as she revealed a baby bump in a stunning blue dress made of roses. Bianca Belair made a surprise return to announced that she is pregnant in a feel-good moment. Some fans may consider this heartwarming announcement as bittersweet since Belair had previously been out of action for an entire year following a finger injury. Now with child, Bianca will remain sidelined for the better part of nine months. “The EST is having a baby!” announced Belair to a giant reaction. WrestleMania 42 host John Cena, was in the ring for the announcement. After Cena announced the WrestleMania attendance of 50,617, Cena joked that the new WrestleMania attendance is 50,618 to include “the youngest WWE Superstar in history.” Belair, who just turned 37, is married to fellow WWE Superstar and former tag team champion Montez Ford. The two starred in the WWE reality series Love and WWE. Given the omnipresence of WWE Superstars in the Hollywood-led TKO era, a reality series chronicling the EST’s pregnancy would be a welcomed addition to WWE’s enviable empire of content. Some fans speculated that Bianca would get involved in tomorrow’s heated showdown between the EST’s former WrestleMania opponent Rhea Ripley and former WrestleMania tag team partner Jade Cargill. With Bianca physically unable to compete, those plans will be shelved for the greater good. Bianca and Jade’s third partner from WrestleMania 40, Naomi, announced her pregnancy last year. According to a recent interview on “Hot Ones” featuring Jey Uso and his twin brother—Naomi’s husband Jimmy—the new baby is here. WrestleMania’s main event features two multi-generational talents. Second-generation Undisputed WWE champion Cody Rhodes is defending his title against third-generation 14-time world champion Randy Orton. With WWE in the midst of a Black renaissance, future hall of fame talent like Bianca and Naomi are likely laying the groundwork for something that is virtually unheard of in WWE, let alone pro wrestling in general: Second-generation Black talent.
